item.title: Damian Lillard's Stunning Comeback: 3-Point King Returns
item.description:
Damian Lillard’s Stunning Comeback: 3-Point King Returns

Here’s a fact almost no one saw coming: a 35-year-old guard, more than a year removed from a torn Achilles, walked onto an All-Star floor and beat two of the league’s deadliest shooters. Damian Lillard didn’t just compete in the 2026 3-Point Contest — he won it.

That single night reminded everyone why “Dame Time” still echoes around the NBA. It also raised a bigger question: what does Lillard’s recovery mean for a Portland Trail Blazers team that is suddenly reshaping its entire roster?

item.title: Jerami Grant Trade Talk: Surprising Truth Behind Portland's $160M Star
item.description:
What if the Portland Trail Blazers’ highest-paid player is also the one most likely to be moved this summer? That’s the uncomfortable question swirling around Jerami Grant as the 2026 NBA playoffs unfold and Portland’s front office begins shaping the roster around a returning Damian Lillard.

Quick Summary: Jerami Grant is averaging 18.6 points per game on 38.9% from three this season, but his playoff minutes have shrunk to 20 or fewer per game following a calf strain. With a contract reportedly worth around $160 million, he is now at the center of trade speculation as Portland searches for a third star to pair with Lillard and Deni Avdija.

item.title: Rayan Rupert's Surprising Rise: From Blazers Cast-Off to Grizzlies Starter
item.description:
What happens when an NBA team gives up on a 21-year-old too soon? The Memphis Grizzlies might have found the answer — and the Portland Trail Blazers might be regretting the question.

Rayan Rupert, the French-born guard-forward who was waived by Portland in February 2026, has quietly transformed into a legitimate rotation piece for Memphis. In just five starts with the Grizzlies, he’s averaging 10.4 points and 5.8 rebounds in 26.8 minutes per game — numbers that dwarf anything he produced in Portland.
